correctness.rationale: Each nonidentity output determines its first and last changed positions; mass balance on the chosen block leaves an anagram on that smaller interval. Any interval of length at most k extends to a legal length-k block for n≥k. Inclusion–exclusion for the two fixed ends in a uniform multiset ordering gives T(v), including identical endpoint letters. Counting labeled realizations bounds T(v) by f_m, strictly for repeats since each allowed ordering has at least two realizations and f_m>0. Hence all length-k windows must be injective for global equality, and after the first k positions each next symbol has q−k+1 choices. For binary k=3, different outputs correspond to unequal pairs separated by one or two sites; their count is the sum of consecutive difference bits and adjacent XORs of those bits. Grouping differences into pairs bounds each pair contribution by two and each bridge by one. At odd n, equality permits all (1,0), all (0,1), or a single (1,1) between a (1,0) prefix and (0,1) suffix; at even n the terminal contribution forces all pairs (1,0) and a final one. Doubling for the initial bit gives the asserted counts. Appending b after a contributes z^(b+(a XOR b)), giving the displayed generating polynomial. The 2n−3 distinct nonzero linear forms in independent uniform differences are fair and pairwise independent, giving the mean and variance exactly. I used the proof, not the frozen script; its longer binary ranges compare against the local formula rather than directly enumerated descendants.

originality.rationale: Independent retrieval of the primary Chen–Milenkovic paper shows an exact binary per-center volume formula in the same channel, not just redundancy bounds. Separately, two earlier Resultary findings cover the endpoint-count decomposition and sharp universal bound on its attainable range, and the full length-three distribution, maxima, counts and moments. The apparently larger scope off the attainable bound is a direct use of the existing unrestricted local lemma and strict local bound, not an additional sharp answer for q<k.

value.rationale: Exact channel sphere sizes and sharp optimizing centers are motivated coding-theoretic invariants. As offered, however, the result combines already available exact length-three data with an unrestricted summation of the earlier local endpoint-count lemma. The small-k cases not in the older high-alphabet theorem are elementary or explicitly covered, and the frozen finding leaves the independently interesting smaller-alphabet k≥4 sharp maxima open. There is no surviving distinct scientific contribution of comparable substance in the stated finding.
